A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

patients with nonsense/ frameshift mutations have more severe NF2 disease and are diagnosed earlier than those with other types of mutations, which is consistent with the dominant negative effect of the truncated protein.
patients with NF2 who are found to have nonsense/frameshift or large deletions in the NF2 should be followed up more closely than those with other types of mutations.

patients with nonsense/ frameshift mutations are more likely to have earlier onset of symptoms, more cutaneous lesions, more spinal tumours, more meningiomas, more non-VIII cranio-facial nerve schwannomas and more severe symptoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical phenotype of patients with NF2 is influenced by the type of mutation in the NF2 tumour suppressor gene.
patients with truncating mutations have an earlier onset of NF2 symptoms, more meningiomas, more spinal tumours and more cutaneous lesions.
NF2 patients with nonsense/ frameshift mutations have a more severe disease presentation, which may be due to a greater degree of loss of protein function.
